```{r}
#| include: false
# Data for the decision map, read once at render: every option of the full menu,
# the curve of the claim, the curve of the negative scales, every option set
# against its twins on the curve, and the titles of the pages that teach each
# option. All of it is aggregate. The pairs travel as three short arrays per
# option and test (twin on the curve, r of the alternative, p < 0.05 or not),
# which keeps the page small. The inference rules need no pairs, because the
# curve file carries every p-value.

axes <- c("outcome", "predictor", "copredictor", "estimator", "sample", "weights",
          "construction", "noop", "item_set", "cell_weight", "measure", "pred_form", "family")
vary <- c("outcome", "predictor", "copredictor", "estimator", "noop", "item_set",
          "cell_weight", "measure", "pred_form")

menu <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_options.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
curve <- readr::read_csv("data/spec_curve.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_arrange("r_ca") |>
  datawizard::data_modify(idx = seq_along(r_ca) - 1L)
curve_neg <- readr::read_csv("data/spec_curve_negative.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
deviations <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_deviations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
twin_index <- datawizard::data_select(curve, select = c(axes, "idx"))
pair_rows <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_deviations_rows.csv.gz", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_filter(curve == "positive" & axis != "se") |>
  dplyr::left_join(twin_index, by = axes)
stopifnot(!anyNA(pair_rows$idx), nrow(curve) == 864)

pairs <- pair_rows |>
  datawizard::data_modify(key = paste(axis, option, rule, sep = "|")) |>
  split(~key) |> # r-style: keep – a list named by key is what the map reads
  purrr::map(\(d) list(i = d$idx, r = round(d$r_ca_dev, 4), s = as.integer(d$p_dev < 0.05)))

# the cells and countries left by the two series that do not cover the panel
coverage <- pair_rows |>
  datawizard::data_filter(option %in% c("es_1574_tips", "es_growth")) |>
  dplyr::distinct(option, n_cells_dev, n_countries_dev) |>
  split(~option) |> # r-style: keep – as above
  purrr::map(\(d) list(cells = d$n_cells_dev[1], countries = d$n_countries_dev[1]))

curve_js <- curve |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(vary)), idx,
    r_ca = round(r_ca, 4),
    p_conv = signif(p_conv, 3), p_cr1 = signif(p_cr1, 3), p_cr2 = signif(p_cr2, 3),
    ref = is_reference
  )
neg_js <- curve_neg |>
  dplyr::transmute(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(vary)), r_ca = round(r_ca, 4),
                   p_cr2 = signif(p_cr2, 3))

# page titles without their Markdown emphasis, for the links to the teaching pages
pages <- unique(menu$taught_on) |>
  purrr::set_names() |>
  purrr::map(\(f) gsub("*", "", rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(file.path("../..", f))$title, fixed = TRUE))

ojs_define(menu_raw = menu, curve_raw = curve_js, neg_raw = neg_js, dev_raw = deviations,
           pairs_raw = pairs, coverage_raw = coverage, pages_raw = pages)
```

The map lays out every decision that an analysis of the claim has to make, in the order in which an analyst meets them on the way from the data to a verdict: which country-years enter, how the answers to the survey question become an outcome, which figure stands for poor economic performance, which country-years are compared with which, whose average the slope describes, which model is fitted and how uncertain its answer is said to be. Each decision shows all its options, those that are on the curve of 864 specifications and those that the course teaches but has taken off the curve because they answer another question or answer this one less well, and the map opens on the reproduced specification of the course.

Selecting an option rewrites the estimand statement, with the phrases that the choice changed marked, and opens a description of the option: what it estimates, whether it is a justifiable way of answering the claim, what it does to the results when it is swapped into the specifications of the curve, and where in the course it is taught. The [specification menu](menu.qmd) gives the full reasoning and the evidence behind each option. Nothing is fitted in the browser, and every number is read from the files under `data/` that the course pipeline writes.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Data and constants of the map. This chunk displays nothing: a named cell
// whose value is not a DOM node would otherwise print as an inspector line.
menu = transpose(menu_raw)
curve = transpose(curve_raw)
negCurve = transpose(neg_raw)
devRows = transpose(dev_raw)
VARY = ["outcome", "predictor", "copredictor", "estimator", "noop", "item_set", "cell_weight", "measure", "pred_form"]
ALL_AXES = ["sample", "outcome", "construction", "noop", "item_set", "cell_weight", "predictor", "measure", "pred_form", "estimator", "copredictor", "weights", "family", "se"]
curveKey = d => VARY.map(a => d[a]).join("|")
curveIndex = new Map(curve.map((d, k) => [curveKey(d), k]))
negIndex = new Map(negCurve.map((d, k) => [curveKey(d), k]))

DM = {
  return {
    stages: [
      {id: "data", title: "The data and the sample", note: "Which country-years enter the analysis, and so which population the answer describes.", axes: ["sample"]},
      {id: "outcome", title: "The outcome", note: "How the answers to the question on what the EU means become one number for each country-year.", axes: ["outcome", "construction", "noop", "item_set", "cell_weight"]},
      {id: "predictor", title: "The predictor", note: "Which figure stands for poor national economic performance, and in what form it enters.", axes: ["predictor", "measure", "pred_form"]},
      {id: "comparison", title: "The comparison", note: "Which country-years are compared with which, and what is held fixed while they are compared.", axes: ["estimator", "copredictor"]},
      {id: "average", title: "Whose average", note: "How much each country-year counts in the slope.", axes: ["weights"]},
      {id: "model", title: "The model form", note: "The model that is fitted to the cell means.", axes: ["family"]},
      {id: "inference", title: "The inference", note: "How uncertain the slope is said to be, which decides its class on the curve.", axes: ["se"]}
    ],
    colour: {outcome: "#0e3b6a", construction: "#1f4c7c", predictor: "#2a5d8f", copredictor: "#4a78ab", sample: "#0f6b6b", weights: "#2b8585", estimator: "#8c5a10",
             noop: "#4a7a3f", item_set: "#4a7a3f", cell_weight: "#4a7a3f", measure: "#4a7a3f", pred_form: "#7b6a8f", family: "#7b6a8f", se: "#7b6a8f"},
    levelName: {estimand: "Level 1 – Estimands", measurement: "Level 2 – Measurement", estimation: "Level 3 – Estimation"},
    levelShort: {estimand: "Level 1", measurement: "Level 2", estimation: "Level 3"},
    judgement: {kept: "On the curve", other_question: "Another question", weaker_answer: "A weaker answer", check: "A check"},
    ruleLabel: {cr2: "CR2 errors with Satterthwaite df", re_conventional: "model-based errors", re_cr1_g1: "errors clustered by country (CR1, 26 df)",
                rewb_satterthwaite: "Satterthwaite df", rewb_cr2: "CR2 errors with Satterthwaite df", beta_cr1_g1: "errors clustered by country (CR1, 26 df)",
                mi_rubin_cr1_g1: "a clustered test pooled over ten imputations (26 df)", conventional: "conventional errors", cr1_g1: "errors clustered by country (CR1, 26 df)",
                identical_to_count: "the test of the count"},
    preferredRule: {re: "re_cr1_g1", rewb: "rewb_cr2", beta: "beta_cr1_g1", mi_mice: "mi_rubin_cr1_g1", mi_amelia: "mi_rubin_cr1_g1"},
    sePcol: {cr2: "p_cr2", cr1: "p_cr1", conventional: "p_conv"},
    seDev: {cr1: "cr1_g1", conventional: "conventional"},
    seName: {cr2: "CR2 errors", cr1: "CR1 errors", conventional: "conventional errors"},
    kItems: {all: {mcosmo: 5, mutil: 2, mcomm: 4, mlib: 2, mpos: 7, mneg: 6}, un: {mcosmo: 5, mutil: 2, mcomm: 3, mlib: 2, mpos: 7, mneg: 5}},
    numWord: {2: "two", 3: "three", 4: "four", 5: "five", 6: "six", 7: "seven"},
    negativeOutcomes: ["mcomm", "mlib", "mneg"],
    domainR: [-0.66, 0.32]
  };
}

// numbers as the site prints them: fixed decimals and a true minus sign
fmtR = x => (x < 0 ? "−" : "") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(3)
// four decimals below 0.001 and within 0.005 of the threshold, so that a p
// just above 0.05 never prints as 0.050
fmtP = p => p < 0.0001 ? "< 0.0001" : p < 0.001 || Math.abs(p - 0.05) < 0.005 ? p.toFixed(4) : p.toFixed(3)
// "p = 0.029" or "p < 0.0001", so that a bound never follows an equals sign
pEq = p => p < 0.0001 ? "p < 0.0001" : `p = ${fmtP(p)}`
fmtPct = x => x.toFixed(1) + "%"
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
decisionMap = {
  const opt = (axis, code) => menu.find(d => d.axis === axis && d.option === code);
  const optionsOf = axis => menu.filter(d => d.axis === axis);
  const col = axis => DM.colour[axis];
  const el = (tag, attrs, ...kids) => {
    const n = document.createElement(tag);
    if (attrs) for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(attrs)) {
      if (k === "class") n.className = v;
      else if (k === "text") n.textContent = v;
      else if (k === "style") n.setAttribute("style", v);
      else n.setAttribute(k, v);
    }
    for (const kid of kids) if (kid !== null && kid !== undefined) n.append(kid);
    return n;
  };
  const pageLink = file => el("a", {href: "../../" + file.replace(/\.qmd$/, ".html")}, pages_raw[file] || file);

  // ---- state: one option per decision, starting from the reproduced specification
  const refRow = curve.find(d => d.ref === true);
  const REF = {sample: "all", weights: "none", construction: "share", family: "gaussian", se: "cr2"};
  for (const a of VARY) REF[a] = refRow[a];
  let sel = Object.assign({}, REF);
  let lastOn = Object.assign({}, REF);
  let lastUnempSeries = REF.measure;
  let latest = null;
  let prevText = null;

  const isOn = (s, a) => opt(a, s[a]).on_curve === true;
  const offAxes = s => ALL_AXES.filter(a => !isOn(s, a));

  // the specification on the curve that stands in for every off-curve choice
  // with the last on-curve option of that decision
  function twinOf(s) {
    const t = Object.assign({}, s);
    for (const a of ALL_AXES) if (!isOn(s, a)) t[a] = lastOn[a];
    if (t.predictor === "growth") { t.measure = "wb_growth"; t.pred_form = "raw"; }
    else if (t.measure === "wb_growth" || t.measure === "es_growth") t.measure = lastUnempSeries;
    return t;
  }
  const curveRowOf = s => { const k = curveIndex.get(curveKey(s)); return k === undefined ? null : curve[k]; };

  function choose(axis, code) {
    const prev = Object.assign({}, sel);
    sel[axis] = code;
    if (axis === "predictor") {
      if (code === "growth") { sel.measure = prev.measure === "es_growth" ? "es_growth" : "wb_growth"; sel.pred_form = "raw"; }
      else if (sel.measure === "wb_growth" || sel.measure === "es_growth") sel.measure = lastUnempSeries;
    }
    if (axis === "measure") {
      const growthSeries = code === "wb_growth" || code === "es_growth";
      sel.predictor = growthSeries ? "growth" : "unemp";
      if (growthSeries) sel.pred_form = "raw";
    }
    for (const a of ALL_AXES) if (isOn(sel, a)) lastOn[a] = sel[a];
    if (sel.predictor === "unemp" && isOn(sel, "measure")) lastUnempSeries = sel.measure;
    latest = axis;
  }

  // ---- the estimand statement, as segments that can be compared with the last one
  function statement(s) {
    const o = a => opt(a, s[a]);
    const k = DM.kItems[s.item_set][s.outcome];
    const outcomeText = o("construction").phrase.replace("{frames}", o("outcome").phrase).replace("{k}", DM.numWord[k]);
    let sampleText = o("sample").phrase;
    if (s.measure === "es_1574_tips") {
      const c = coverage_raw.es_1574_tips;
      sampleText = s.sample === "all"
        ? `the ${c.cells} country-years that the Eurostat table tipsun20 covers, from ${c.countries} member states without the United Kingdom and, before 2009, only France and Sweden`
        : `${sampleText}, and of these only the country-years that the Eurostat table tipsun20 covers`;
    }
    if (s.measure === "es_growth") {
      const c = coverage_raw.es_growth;
      sampleText = s.sample === "all"
        ? `the ${c.cells} country-years of the ${c.countries} member states other than the United Kingdom, which the Eurostat growth series does not cover`
        : `${sampleText}, without the United Kingdom`;
    }
    const other = s.predictor === "unemp" ? "GDP growth" : "the unemployment rate";
    const predName = s.predictor === "unemp" ? "unemployment" : "GDP growth";
    const seg = (key, text, lv, colourAxis) => ({key, text, lv, colourAxis: colourAxis || key});
    return {
      question: [
        "Among ", seg("sample", sampleText, "l1"), ", with ", seg("weights", o("weights").phrase, "l1"),
        ", the association between ", seg("predictor", o("predictor").phrase, "l1"),
        " (", seg("measure", o("measure").phrase, "l2"), ") and ", seg("outcome", outcomeText, "l1"),
        " (", seg("item_set", o("item_set").phrase, "l2"), ", ", seg("noop", o("noop").phrase, "l2"), ", ",
        seg("cell_weight", o("cell_weight").phrase, "l2"), "), comparing ", seg("estimator", o("estimator").phrase, "l1"),
        ", ", seg("copredictor", o("copredictor").phrase.replace("{other}", other), "l1"), "."
      ],
      method: [
        "Answered with ", seg("family", o("family").phrase, "l3"), ", ",
        seg("pred_form", o("pred_form").phrase.replace("{pred}", predName), "l3"), ", and tested by ", seg("se", o("se").phrase, "l3"), "."
      ]
    };
  }
  function renderSegments(target, parts) {
    target.replaceChildren();
    for (const p of parts) {
      if (typeof p === "string") { target.append(p); continue; }
      const span = el("span", {class: `dm-seg ${p.lv}`, style: `--c:${col(p.colourAxis)}`, text: p.text});
      const changed = prevText !== null && prevText[p.key] !== undefined && prevText[p.key] !== p.text;
      target.append(changed ? el("mark", {class: "dm-changed"}, span) : span);
    }
  }

  // ---- what the selection gives
  function pairKey(axis, code) {
    const c = axis === "construction" && code === "rate" ? "count" : code;
    const rule = DM.preferredRule[c] || "cr2";
    const key = `${axis}|${c}|${rule}`;
    return pairs_raw[key] ? {key, rule} : null;
  }
  function verdictOf(s) {
    if (s.family === "beta" && s.construction === "count") return {kind: "inadmissible"};
    const off = offAxes(s).filter(a => a !== "se");
    if (off.length === 0) {
      const d = curveRowOf(s);
      const p = d[DM.sePcol[s.se]];
      return {kind: "curve", d, p, rule: s.se};
    }
    if (off.length === 1 && off[0] === "outcome" && DM.negativeOutcomes.includes(s.outcome)) {
      const k = negIndex.get(curveKey(s));
      return {kind: "negative", d: k === undefined ? null : negCurve[k]};
    }
    if (off.length === 1) {
      const a = off[0], pk = pairKey(a, s[a]);
      const twin = curveRowOf(twinOf(s));
      if (pk === null || twin === null) return {kind: "unfitted", axes: off};
      const P = pairs_raw[pk.key];
      const k = P.i.indexOf(twin.idx);
      if (k < 0) return {kind: "outside", axis: a, twin};
      return {kind: "refit", axis: a, rule: pk.rule, r: P.r[k], sig: P.s[k] === 1, twin};
    }
    return {kind: "unfitted", axes: off};
  }

  // ---- the map
  const stageEls = {};
  const chipEls = [];
  const verdictBox = el("p", {class: "dm-verdict", "aria-live": "polite"});
  const resetBtn = el("button", {type: "button", class: "dm-reset"}, "Back to the reproduced specification");
  const stagesBox = el("div", {class: "dm-stages"});
  DM.stages.forEach((st, si) => {
    const box = el("section", {class: "dm-stage", "aria-labelledby": `dm-stage-${st.id}`},
      el("div", {class: "dm-stage-head"}, el("span", {class: "dm-stage-num", "aria-hidden": "true"}, String(si + 1)),
        el("h3", {id: `dm-stage-${st.id}`}, st.title)),
      el("p", {class: "dm-stage-note"}, st.note));
    for (const axis of st.axes) {
      const opts = optionsOf(axis);
      const first = opts[0];
      const nameId = `dm-dec-${axis}`;
      const group = el("div", {class: "dm-chips", role: "group", "aria-labelledby": nameId});
      for (const o of opts) {
        const tip = o.on_curve ? `${o.label}: on the curve` : `${o.label}: off the curve, taught on ${pages_raw[o.taught_on] || o.taught_on}`;
        const b = el("button", {type: "button", class: "dm-chip" + (o.on_curve ? "" : " off"), style: `--c:${col(axis)}`,
                                "aria-pressed": "false", title: tip, "aria-label": tip, "data-tip": tip}, o.label);
        b.addEventListener("click", () => {
          if (b.getAttribute("aria-disabled") === "true") return;
          const before = b.getBoundingClientRect().top;
          choose(axis, o.option);
          update(st.id);
          const after = b.getBoundingClientRect().top;
          if (Math.abs(after - before) > 1) window.scrollBy(0, after - before);
        });
        chipEls.push({b, axis, code: o.option});
        group.append(b);
      }
      box.append(el("div", {class: "dm-decision"},
        el("div", {class: "dm-decision-name", id: nameId}, first.decision,
          el("span", {class: "lv", style: `color:${col(axis)}`}, DM.levelShort[first.level])),
        group));
    }
    stageEls[st.id] = box;
    stagesBox.append(box);
  });
  const verdictStage = el("section", {class: "dm-stage", "aria-labelledby": "dm-stage-verdict"},
    el("div", {class: "dm-stage-head"}, el("span", {class: "dm-stage-num", "aria-hidden": "true"}, String(DM.stages.length + 1)),
      el("h3", {id: "dm-stage-verdict"}, "The verdict")),
    verdictBox, resetBtn);
  stagesBox.append(verdictStage);
  resetBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const before = resetBtn.getBoundingClientRect().top;
    sel = Object.assign({}, REF); lastOn = Object.assign({}, REF); lastUnempSeries = REF.measure;
    latest = null; update(null);
    const after = resetBtn.getBoundingClientRect().top;
    if (Math.abs(after - before) > 1) window.scrollBy(0, after - before);
  });

  // ---- the panel: statement, the selected option, its twins, the curve
  const statementP = el("p", {class: "dm-statement", "aria-live": "polite"});
  const methodP = el("p", {class: "dm-method"});
  const changedNote = el("p", {class: "dm-small"});
  const optionBox = el("div");
  const pairBox = el("div");
  const curveBox = el("div");
  const panel = el("div", {class: "dm-panel", role: "region", "aria-label": "The selection and its results"},
    el("h3", {}, "The estimand statement"), statementP, methodP, changedNote,
    el("h3", {}, "The selected option"), optionBox,
    el("h3", {}, "Against its twins on the curve"), pairBox,
    el("h3", {}, "The curve of 864"), curveBox);
  const side = el("div", {class: "dm-side"});
  const topSlot = el("div");
  const layout = el("div", {class: "dm-layout"}, el("div", {}, topSlot, stagesBox), side);

  const legend = el("div", {class: "dm-legend"},
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#0e3b6a"}), el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#0f6b6b"}), el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#8c5a10"}), DM.levelName.estimand),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#4a7a3f"}), DM.levelName.measurement),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#7b6a8f"}), DM.levelName.estimation),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "chip-sample"}, "solid"), "on the curve"),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "chip-sample off"}, "dashed"), "in the course, off the curve"));

  const wide = window.matchMedia("(min-width: 1100px)");
  function place(stageId) {
    if (wide.matches) { if (panel.parentNode !== side) side.append(panel); return; }
    if (stageId === null || stageId === undefined) { if (panel.parentNode !== topSlot) topSlot.append(panel); return; }
    const anchor = stageId === "verdict" ? verdictStage : stageEls[stageId];
    if (anchor.nextSibling !== panel) anchor.after(panel);
  }

  // ---- charts
  const recipe = d => VARY.map(a => opt(a, d[a]).label).join("; ");
  function curveChart(width, v) {
    const onAxes = VARY.filter(a => isOn(sel, a));
    const match = curve.filter(d => onAxes.every(a => d[a] === sel[a]));
    const matchSet = new Set(match.map(d => d.idx));
    const showLatest = latest !== null && VARY.includes(latest) && isOn(sel, latest);
    const latestRows = showLatest ? curve.filter(d => d[latest] === sel[latest] && !matchSet.has(d.idx)) : [];
    const latestSet = new Set(latestRows.map(d => d.idx));
    const base = curve.filter(d => !matchSet.has(d.idx) && !latestSet.has(d.idx));
    const x = d => d.idx + 1;
    const dots = (data, stroke, opSig, opNs, r, sw) => [
      Plot.dot(data.filter(d => d.p_cr2 < 0.05), {x, y: "r_ca", r, symbol: "circle", fill: "none", stroke, strokeOpacity: opSig, strokeWidth: sw, title: d => `${recipe(d)}\nr = ${fmtR(d.r_ca)}, CR2 ${pEq(d.p_cr2)}`}),
      Plot.dot(data.filter(d => d.p_cr2 >= 0.05), {x, y: "r_ca", r, symbol: "times", fill: "none", stroke, strokeOpacity: opNs, strokeWidth: sw, title: d => `${recipe(d)}\nr = ${fmtR(d.r_ca)}, CR2 ${pEq(d.p_cr2)}`})
    ];
    const ref = curve.filter(d => d.ref === true);
    const marks = [
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#9aa8b3", strokeWidth: 0.8}),
      ...dots(base, "#1d2731", 0.25, 0.12, 3.6, 0.7),
      ...dots(latestRows, col(latest || "outcome"), 0.65, 0.5, 3.6, 0.9),
      ...dots(match, "#8b1538", 1, 1, 5.5, 1.6),
      Plot.text(ref, {x, y: "r_ca", text: () => "reproduced", dy: 16, fontSize: 10, fill: "#1d2731"})
    ];
    if (v.kind === "refit") {
      marks.push(Plot.ruleY([v.r], {stroke: "#8b1538", strokeDasharray: "4,3", strokeWidth: 1}));
      marks.push(Plot.text([v.r], {x: 860, y: d => d, text: () => `refitted: r = ${fmtR(v.r)}`, textAnchor: "end", dy: -6, fontSize: 10, fill: "#8b1538"}));
    }
    return Plot.plot({
      width, height: Math.max(230, Math.min(320, Math.round(width * 0.5))), marginLeft: 46, marginRight: 10, marginBottom: 38,
      style: {fontSize: "11px", background: "transparent"},
      ariaLabel: "The curve of 864 specifications, with the current selection marked",
      x: {domain: [0, 865], label: "864 specifications, ranked by claim-aligned r →", ticks: 4},
      y: {domain: DM.domainR, label: "↑ Claim-aligned partial r", grid: true, ticks: 5},
      marks
    });
  }
  function pairData(axis, code) {
    if (axis === "se") {
      const yCol = DM.sePcol[code];
      const xCol = code === "cr2" ? "p_conv" : "p_cr2";
      return curve.map(d => {
        const xv = Math.max(d[xCol], 1e-4), yv = Math.max(d[yCol], 1e-4);
        const cx = d.r_ca < 0 && d[xCol] < 0.05, cy = d.r_ca < 0 && d[yCol] < 0.05;
        return {x: xv, y: yv, s: d[yCol] < 0.05, changed: cx !== cy, twin: d, label: recipe(d)};
      });
    }
    const pk = pairKey(axis, code);
    if (pk === null) return null;
    const P = pairs_raw[pk.key];
    return P.i.map((ti, k) => {
      const t = curve[ti];
      const twinClass = t.r_ca < 0 && t.p_cr2 < 0.05, devClass = P.r[k] < 0 && P.s[k] === 1;
      return {x: t.r_ca, y: P.r[k], s: P.s[k] === 1, changed: twinClass !== devClass, twin: t, label: recipe(t)};
    });
  }
  function pairChart(width, axis, code, data, isSelPair) {
    const isSe = axis === "se";
    const same = data.filter(d => !d.changed), moved = data.filter(d => d.changed);
    const selPair = data.filter(d => isSelPair(d.twin));
    const c = col(axis);
    const dots = (rows, stroke, op, r, sw) => [
      Plot.dot(rows.filter(d => d.s), {x: "x", y: "y", r, symbol: "circle", fill: "none", stroke, strokeOpacity: op, strokeWidth: sw, title: d => `${d.label}\n${fmtR(d.x)} → ${fmtR(d.y)}`}),
      Plot.dot(rows.filter(d => !d.s), {x: "x", y: "y", r, symbol: "times", fill: "none", stroke, strokeOpacity: op * 0.8, strokeWidth: sw, title: d => `${d.label}\n${fmtR(d.x)} → ${fmtR(d.y)}`})
    ];
    const lo = isSe ? 1e-4 : DM.domainR[0], hi = isSe ? 1 : DM.domainR[1];
    const xName = isSe ? (code === "cr2" ? "p under conventional errors" : "p under CR2, the rule of the curve") : "claim-aligned r on the curve";
    const yName = isSe ? `p under ${DM.seName[code]}` : "claim-aligned r with this option";
    return Plot.plot({
      width, height: Math.max(240, Math.min(360, Math.round(width * 0.62))), marginLeft: 50, marginRight: 12, marginBottom: 40,
      style: {fontSize: "11px", background: "transparent"},
      ariaLabel: `Each specification on the curve set against the same specification with ${opt(axis, code).label}`,
      x: isSe ? {type: "log", domain: [lo, hi], label: `${xName} →`, ticks: 4, tickFormat: "~g"} : {domain: [lo, hi], label: `${xName} →`, ticks: 5},
      y: isSe ? {type: "log", domain: [lo, hi], label: `↑ ${yName}`, ticks: 4, tickFormat: "~g"} : {domain: [lo, hi], label: `↑ ${yName}`, ticks: 5},
      marks: [
        isSe ? Plot.ruleX([0.05], {stroke: "#9aa8b3", strokeDasharray: "3,3"}) : Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: "#9aa8b3", strokeWidth: 0.8}),
        isSe ? Plot.ruleY([0.05], {stroke: "#9aa8b3", strokeDasharray: "3,3"}) : Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#9aa8b3", strokeWidth: 0.8}),
        Plot.line([[lo, lo], [hi, hi]], {stroke: "#5b6b78", strokeDasharray: "4,3", strokeWidth: 0.8}),
        ...dots(same, "#1d2731", 0.3, 3.4, 0.7),
        ...dots(moved, c, 0.75, 3.4, 0.9),
        ...dots(selPair, "#8b1538", 1, 6, 1.8)
      ]
    });
  }

  // ---- the selected option, in words and numbers
  const curveShares = {
    below: 100 * d3.mean(curve, d => d.r_ca < 0 ? 1 : 0),
    sig: 100 * d3.mean(curve, d => d.r_ca < 0 && d.p_cr2 < 0.05 ? 1 : 0)
  };
  function summaryText(axis, code, o) {
    const negative = axis === "outcome" && DM.negativeOutcomes.includes(code);
    const devCode = axis === "se" ? DM.seDev[code] : code;
    const rows = devRows.filter(d => d.curve === (negative ? "negative" : "positive") && d.axis === axis && d.option === devCode);
    const out = [];
    if (negative) {
      const r = rows[0];
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, `The curve of this claim holds no specification of this scale. On the curve of the negative scales, aligned so that below zero is the direction of the other half of the hypothesis, its 288 specifications lie below zero in ${fmtPct(r.below_zero)} of cases and below zero with CR2 p < 0.05 in ${fmtPct(r.below_zero_sig)}, with a median claim-aligned r of ${fmtR(r.median_r_ca)}.`));
      return out;
    }
    if (axis === "se" && code === "cr2") {
      const conv = 100 * d3.mean(curve, d => d.r_ca < 0 && d.p_conv < 0.05 ? 1 : 0);
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, `Every point of the curve is classed by this rule: ${fmtPct(curveShares.sig)} of the 864 specifications lie below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, against ${fmtPct(conv)} under conventional errors. The partial correlation is the same under every rule, so only the class moves.`));
      return out;
    }
    const withPairs = rows.filter(r => r.n_pairs > 0);
    if (withPairs.length === 0) {
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, code === "wb_growth"
        ? "This is the only growth series on the curve, so there is no other series on the curve to set it against; the Eurostat growth series is compared with it."
        : `Every specification on the curve uses this option, so there is nothing on the curve to set it against; the alternatives on the map are compared with it. On the curve itself ${fmtPct(curveShares.below)} of the 864 specifications lie below zero and ${fmtPct(curveShares.sig)} below zero with CR2 p < 0.05.`));
      return out;
    }
    for (const r of withPairs) {
      const rule = DM.ruleLabel[r.rule] || r.rule;
      const lead = o.on_curve
        ? `Among the ${r.n_pairs} pairs of specifications on the curve that differ only in this decision, the specifications with this option lie below zero in ${fmtPct(r.below_zero)} of cases and below zero with p < 0.05 under ${rule} in ${fmtPct(r.below_zero_sig)}.`
        : `Swapped into the ${r.n_pairs} specifications of the curve to which it applies, this option leaves ${fmtPct(r.below_zero)} of them below zero and ${fmtPct(r.below_zero_sig)} below zero with p < 0.05 under ${rule}, against ${fmtPct(curveShares.sig)} on the curve itself.`;
      const rest = axis === "se"
        ? ` The partial correlations stay as they are, so only the class can move, and it moves for ${fmtPct(r.class_changes)} of the specifications.`
        : ` Their median claim-aligned r is ${fmtR(r.median_r_ca)}, a median shift of ${fmtR(r.median_shift)} from their twins; ${fmtPct(r.sign_changes)} of the pairs change sign and ${fmtPct(r.class_changes)} change class.`;
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, lead + rest));
    }
    if (withPairs.some(r => r.rule !== "cr2" && axis !== "se"))
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-small"}, "Part of the change of class comes from the test, because this option is tested by a different rule from the CR2 rule of the curve."));
    return out;
  }

  function renderOption(width, v, twinSel) {
    optionBox.replaceChildren();
    pairBox.replaceChildren();
    if (latest === null) {
      optionBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, "The map opens on the reproduced specification: the cosmopolitan share on World Bank unemployment, compared within countries net of the common yearly changes, with respondents who mention nothing scored zero, all 13 items and cells as interviewed. Select any option on the map to read what it estimates and whether it answers the claim."));
      pairBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, "Once an option is selected, a chart here sets each specification on the curve against the same specification with that option."));
      return;
    }
    const axis = latest, code = sel[axis], o = opt(axis, code), c = col(axis);
    optionBox.append(
      el("p", {class: "dm-option-title"}, `${o.decision}: ${o.label}`),
      el("span", {class: "dm-badge", style: `--c:${c}`}, DM.levelName[o.level]),
      el("span", {class: "dm-badge" + (o.on_curve ? "" : " off"), style: `--c:${o.on_curve ? "#1d2731" : "#8b1538"}`}, DM.judgement[o.judgement]),
      el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, el("b", {}, "What it estimates. "), o.estimates),
      el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, el("b", {}, o.on_curve ? "Why it is on the curve. " : "Why it is off the curve. "), o.explanation),
      el("p", {class: "dm-small"}, "Taught on ", pageLink(o.taught_on), "."));
    for (const p of summaryText(axis, code, o)) pairBox.append(p);
    const data = DM.negativeOutcomes.includes(code) && axis === "outcome" ? null : pairData(axis, code);
    if (data !== null && data.length > 0) {
      const box = el("div", {class: "dm-chart"});
      // the pairs of the selection: twins that match it on every decision but this
      // one (the series and form follow a change of predictor)
      const free = a => a === axis || (axis === "predictor" && (a === "measure" || a === "pred_form"));
      const isSelPair = t => twinSel !== null && VARY.every(a => free(a) || t[a] === twinSel[a]);
      box.append(pairChart(width, axis, code, data, isSelPair));
      pairBox.append(box);
      const label = o.label;
      const caption = axis === "se"
        ? `Each mark is one of the 864 specifications on the curve, placed by its p-value under ${code === "cr2" ? "conventional errors" : "CR2, the rule of the curve"} (horizontal) and under ${DM.seName[code]} (vertical), on logarithmic scales; values below 0.0001 are drawn at 0.0001. The dashed lines mark p = 0.05 and the diagonal marks equal p-values. Circles are significant at 5% on the vertical rule, crosses are not; coloured marks change class (below zero with p < 0.05, or not) between the two rules. The burgundy mark is the specification of the current selection.`
        : `Each mark is one pair: a specification on the curve, placed horizontally by its claim-aligned partial r, and the same specification with ${label}, placed vertically. Marks on the dashed diagonal are unchanged, and marks below it lie further in the direction of the claim. Circles are significant at 5% under the test of the option, crosses are not; coloured marks change class (below zero with p < 0.05, or not) between the two members of the pair. The burgundy mark is the pair of the current selection, where there is one.`;
      pairBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-caption"}, caption));
    }
  }

  function renderVerdict(v) {
    const parts = [];
    const sym = sig => sig ? "an open circle, significant at 5%" : "a cross, not significant at 5%";
    if (v.kind === "curve") {
      const d = v.d, k = d.idx;
      const ruleTxt = v.rule === "cr2" ? "CR2" : DM.seName[v.rule];
      parts.push(`The selection is one of the 864 specifications on the curve: claim-aligned r = ${fmtR(d.r_ca)}, ${ruleTxt} ${pEq(v.p)}.`);
      if (v.rule !== "cr2") parts.push(` The curve classes it by CR2, ${pEq(d.p_cr2)}, which draws it as ${sym(d.p_cr2 < 0.05)}.`);
      else parts.push(` On the curve it is ${sym(d.p_cr2 < 0.05)}.`);
      parts.push(` On the curve, ${fmtPct(100 * k / 864)} of the specifications lie further in the direction of the claim.`);
      if (sel.predictor === "growth") parts.push(" The sign of growth is reversed on the curve, because the claim expects framing to rise with growth.");
      return parts.join("");
    }
    const off = offAxes(sel).filter(a => a !== "se");
    const why = off.map(a => `${opt(a, sel[a]).decision.toLowerCase()} – ${opt(a, sel[a]).label} (${DM.judgement[opt(a, sel[a]).judgement].toLowerCase()})`).join("; ");
    if (v.kind === "inadmissible") return "A count is a number of items, not a proportion, so the beta family cannot model it, and the menu holds no such analysis.";
    let txt = `The curve holds no analysis with this selection, because of ${off.length === 1 ? "one choice" : "these choices"}: ${why}. The burgundy marks are the specifications on the curve that share every other choice.`;
    if (v.kind === "negative" && v.d) txt += ` On the curve of the negative scales this specification has claim-aligned r = ${fmtR(v.d.r_ca)} and CR2 ${pEq(v.d.p_cr2)}, aligned so that below zero is the direction of the other half of the hypothesis.`;
    if (v.kind === "refit") txt += ` Refitted with this option, the closest specification on the curve moves from r = ${fmtR(v.twin.r_ca)} to r = ${fmtR(v.r)}, ${v.sig ? "with p < 0.05" : "with p ≥ 0.05"} under ${DM.ruleLabel[v.rule]}; the dashed line marks where that refit would sit.`;
    if (v.kind === "outside") txt += " This option was fitted only at the standard measurement settings (raw unemployment in the World Bank series, all items, cells as interviewed), and the selection differs from them, so no refit of it exists.";
    if (v.kind === "unfitted" && off.length > 1) txt += " Each option off the curve was fitted one at a time against the curve, so this combination of options was never fitted.";
    return txt;
  }

  let lastWidth = 0;
  function drawPanel() {
    const width = Math.max(280, Math.floor(panel.clientWidth - 34));
    lastWidth = width;
    const v = verdictOf(sel);
    const twin = curveRowOf(offAxes(sel).filter(a => a !== "se").length === 0 ? sel : twinOf(sel));
    renderOption(width, v, twin);
    curveBox.replaceChildren();
    const box = el("div", {class: "dm-chart"});
    box.append(curveChart(width, v));
    curveBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, renderVerdict(v)), box,
      el("p", {class: "dm-caption"}, `Each mark is one of the 864 specifications on the curve of the claim, ranked by its claim-aligned partial r, where below zero is the direction of the claim. Open circles are significant at 5% under CR2 errors clustered by country, crosses are not. Burgundy marks are the specifications that match every on-curve choice of the selection${latest !== null && VARY.includes(latest) && isOn(sel, latest) ? `, and the coloured marks are the other specifications that share the option selected last (${opt(latest, sel[latest]).label})` : ""}. The ink label marks the reproduced specification.`));
  }

  function update(stageId) {
    for (const {b, axis, code} of chipEls) {
      b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", sel[axis] === code ? "true" : "false");
      const disabled = axis === "pred_form" && code === "log" && sel.predictor === "growth";
      b.setAttribute("aria-disabled", disabled ? "true" : "false");
      const tip = disabled ? "Logged: growth takes negative values, so it enters raw only" : b.getAttribute("data-tip");
      b.title = tip;
      b.setAttribute("aria-label", tip);
    }
    const st = statement(sel);
    renderSegments(statementP, st.question);
    renderSegments(methodP, st.method);
    const nowText = {};
    for (const p of [...st.question, ...st.method]) if (typeof p !== "string") nowText[p.key] = p.text;
    const anyChanged = prevText !== null && Object.keys(nowText).some(k => prevText[k] !== nowText[k]);
    changedNote.textContent = anyChanged
      ? "The marked phrases are the ones that the latest choice changed. Bold phrases state the question (Level 1), green phrases say how its variables are measured (Level 2), and the second sentence says how the answer is reached (Level 3)."
      : "Bold phrases state the question (Level 1), green phrases say how its variables are measured (Level 2), and the second sentence says how the answer is reached (Level 3).";
    prevText = nowText;
    const v = verdictOf(sel);
    verdictBox.textContent = v.kind === "curve"
      ? `On the curve: r = ${fmtR(v.d.r_ca)}, ${v.rule === "cr2" ? "CR2" : DM.seName[v.rule]} ${pEq(v.p)}${v.rule === "cr2" ? "" : ` (CR2 ${pEq(v.d.p_cr2)})`}.`
      : v.kind === "refit" ? `Off the curve. Refitted with this option: r = ${fmtR(v.r)}, ${v.sig ? "p < 0.05" : "p ≥ 0.05"} under ${DM.ruleLabel[v.rule]}.`
      : "Off the curve: the course holds no fitted analysis for this combination.";
    place(stageId);
    drawPanel();
  }

  const root = el("div", {class: "dm"}, legend, layout);
  update(null);
  const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => {
    const w = Math.floor(panel.clientWidth - 34);
    if (w > 0 && Math.abs(w - lastWidth) > 24) { place(latest === null ? null : (DM.stages.find(s => s.axes.includes(latest)) || {}).id); drawPanel(); }
  });
  ro.observe(root);
  const onMedia = () => { place(latest === null ? null : (DM.stages.find(s => s.axes.includes(latest)) || {}).id); drawPanel(); };
  wide.addEventListener("change", onMedia);
  invalidation.then(() => { ro.disconnect(); wide.removeEventListener("change", onMedia); });
  return root;
}
```

The three levels of the map are those of the [specification menu](menu.qmd#level-estimand): a Level 1 choice changes the question, a Level 2 choice changes how its variables are measured, and a Level 3 choice changes how the answer is reached. Two of the measurement choices change more than their place on the map suggests, and the estimand statement records it. The rule for respondents who mention nothing is set where the outcome is built, yet scoring them zero lets the rate of saying nothing enter every scale, so that the outcome becomes a mixture of framing and of the willingness to name any meaning at all. A published series that covers only part of the panel is chosen where the predictor is measured, yet it changes the population of the question as well, which is why selecting the Eurostat table tipsun20 marks the sample phrase of the statement too.
